citations.assessment: R. Simon in the name of R. Yehoshua ben Levi gives the analogy of a king omitting a bad legion’s name on the subject of the second day.

The two cited chapters independently give the chain. Chapter 10 depicts creation continuing to stretch out; chapter 39 gives the king remaining bowed during prayer. The anchor leads to the first of the two preserved loci.
Simon cites Yehoshua ben Levi about the interpretive purpose of Chronicles, alongside a second transmission.
The exact chain warns against taking the mitzvah of the poor lightly. The chapter also has a distinct transmission from Simon in Elazar’s name.
Chapter 12 explicitly gives Simon transmitting Yehoshua ben Levi in the account of the sanctuary. Nearby Yehudah bar Simon occurrences are distinct.
The priestly robe passage gives Simon in Natan’s name on the two transgressions for which the Torah assigned atonement.
Simon’s named chain from Shimon ben Ḥalafta gives a parable of someone brought up in the royal household.

holds.reason: Chapter 4 contains a teaching by Yehoshua ben Levi about Elazar without Simon in the checked text. The exact Simon chain occurs in chapter 2 on a different topic. Preserve chapter 4 pending an exact match or print collation.
The checked chapter 10 has no exact chain. Chapter 5 gives Simon in Yehoshua ben Levi’s name on trusting God. Without knowing which context Heilprin intended, leave the printed 10 unlinked.
